newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank seen selling markka at 2.98 per mark.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank seen selling markka at 2.98 per mark.

text.p: The Bank of Finland intervened in the foreign exchange market on Thursday selling markka for German marks at around 2.98 markka per mark, forex dealers in Helsinki said.
"The central bank has been in the market today selling markka at around 2.98 (per mark)," one senior forex dealer said.
At the Bank of Finland, a senior official at the market intervention department declined comment.
At 1059/0759 GMT, the markka was at 2.9830 per mark compared with Wednesday's close at 2.9870.
Central bank intervention had been expected, dealers said earlier on Thursday morning.
The Bank of Finland was seen attempting to prevent the markka from firming before a potential decision later this autumn to link the Finnish unit to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

The markka has been strengthening gradually since late August, boosted by healthy macro-economic fundamentals. Finnish exporters are converting sizeable foreign currency earnings into markka creating strong demand for the markka, analysts said.
The Bank of Finland's stated policy is to allow the markka to float freely but to cushion excessively sharp intra-day moves, which could be regarded as lack of currency stability.
